findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the advertised backpressure does not exist
findings.body: Each per-queue `queue.Queue()` is created without a maxsize, and `submit` calls `work_queue.put` without blocking limits. The class docstring of `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but nothing ever fills up. If a slow downstream handler or a stalled worker falls behind, in-memory work items and their Kafka message payloads accumulate without bound while the consumer keeps polling and fetching. Either bound the queues and make submit block or apply poll-side pausing, or remove the claim from the docstring.

findings.title: A never-arriving offset stalls commits for the partition permanently
findings.body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Offsets can legitimately skip on compacted or transactional topics, or when a message is dropped before submit. When that happens, the highest committable offset can never advance past the hole because the missing offset is never added. Commits for that partition then stop until restart, and the consumer group's lag grows indefinitely. The skipped offset should be treated as complete, for example by tracking the next expected offset from the broker rather than assuming contiguity.

findings.title: Kafka commit function is invoked from a background thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` runs on its own thread and calls `self.commit_function`, which calls the arroyo `commit` callable provided by the StreamProcessor. The rest of the arroyo pipeline (and the consumer) is driven from the processor thread, and the commit callable and the Kafka consumer are not documented as thread-safe. Calling commit concurrently with poll or with rebalance handling can cause races or errors during partition reassignment. Commits should be issued from the processing thread, for example in `poll`.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of what its name and the design promise
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` is named to check that errors do not block offset commits, and the worker's `finally` marks a failed item as complete. So offset 101 is committed after 100 fails. The test instead asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which requires no commit. The check also runs only 0.2s after processing, before the 1s commit loop runs, so it passes by timing rather than by design. The assertion should verify that the commit reaches 102 (the next offset after 101), and the sleep should be replaced by a wait for the commit.

findings.title: Tests rely on fixed sleeps and polling of internal queue stats, which makes them flaky
findings.body: Most new thread-queue tests poll `queue_pool.get_stats()` and `call_count` in loops with `time.sleep(0.1)`, then assert the result without any event. The commit tests can pass before the 1-second commit thread has run, and `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps` only checks commits that happened to occur within the window. Use threading events or the `wait` helpers already used in queue_consumer tests so the tests are deterministic instead of depending on scheduler timing.

findings.title: Kafka integration test leaks processor and topic on assertion failure and bypasses the factory it claims to test
findings.body: The processor is shut down only on the success path, and the factory is shut down there too, so a failed assertion leaves the StreamProcessor and its queue threads running. The `KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES` override is also set but never used by the StreamProcessor, which takes the topic explicitly, so the override is misleading. The `finally` block only deletes the topic and swallows all exceptions. Move processor and factory cleanup into `finally`, and remove the unused override.
